text: hey so i have this 5 slider deej homemade thing and im wondering how, if at all, could we map it to something like brush sizes inside of the @cart/editor/ if thats even possible; because it is not a digital dial and is physical, i would have to behave in a way where it can fall back to not being enforced through the interface obviously but idk if the part where u enforce it thru the interface is possible. i assume its gotta be a like to the midi controller we have
resolution: Built the full deej vertical: framework/deej.zig reads the homemade 5-fader board as plain POSIX serial (no MIDI/ALSA needed — deej boards print |-separated 10-bit values over /dev/ttyACM*), with a movement-only contract so the physical faders never fight the UI: events fire only when a fader physically moves past the jitter threshold, the first line after connect is a silent baseline, and no board = zero events with the interface exactly as before (the fallback you asked about IS the design). __deej_* bindings + has-deej ingredient flip source-driven from the new runtime/hooks/useDeej.ts door; in cart/editor, fader 1 drives brush size (1..128, same range as the toolbar slider) and fader 2 drives flow while a paint surface is up. Verified with 6 parser unit tests, a live pty fake-board harness, and headless shots with and without a board. Faders 3-5 left unmapped pending your pick. NOTE: user is not in the dialout group — needs 'sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER' + relogin before the real board is readable, and the deej desktop volume app must not hold the port at the same time (serial is single-consumer).
